words.gloss_range: continuing conjunction that carries the ownership claim forward inside the reported sequence
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) makes the ayah begin as continuation before the worship premise is asserted. The reader hears the prohibition as part of the surah's accumulating testimony, not as a detached legal aside. Its light bound form also lets connection arrive before assertion, so continuity is the first signal at the boundary.

topics.headline: continuation inside reported testimony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ownership claim remains inside the surah's unfolding declaration chain rather than starting as an isolated rule.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a conjunction, and the following clause is locally parsed as part of the asserted sequence.

topics.headline: light connector before assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a small connective glide into the assertive clause, making the boundary feel linked and newly emphatic at the same time.
topics.reason: The single-letter proclitic stands before the assertive particle, so the surface foregrounds linkage before the premise expands.

words.gloss_range: annulling assertive particle embedding the mosque-ownership clause as governed reported content
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّ}} ({{tr:anna}}) governs the ownership statement and makes it serious reported content before the prohibition arrives. The accepted independence variant shows how forceful the claim can sound, but the local reading keeps the premise embedded in the preceding disclosure. The nominal premise is therefore settled first; only then does the command regulate invocation. The boundary also moves from the warning of 72:17 into sacred ownership without severing the report chain.

topics.headline: embedded claim with variant contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the mosque-ownership claim is grammatically embedded in reported disclosure while still carrying emphatic doctrinal force.
topics.reason: The local particle governs the nominal clause, while the accepted variant contrast confirms that independence is a discourse-force contrast rather than a replacement of the local parse.

topics.headline: settled ownership before prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees conduct answer a prior state of belonging, not a command presented without a premise.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence parses the first clause as a nominal ownership claim and the second clause as its consequent prohibition.

topics.headline: warning scene to ownership scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the boundary move from the warning of 72:17 into a sacred-ownership premise without severing the report chain.
topics.reason: The particle reopens the declaration chain after 72:17 and introduces the clause that grounds the current prohibition.

words.gloss_range: definite plural prostration-loci or mosques as worship-sites gathered under divine ownership
words.root_gloss_range: prostration, bodily lowering, and the locus or occasion where that act is performed; local form selects the place-locus noun
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمَسَٰجِدَ}} ({{tr:al-masājida}}) is definite and plural, so the premise gathers the class of prostration-sites rather than one local building. Its place-noun form keeps bodily lowering inside the idea of the site: worship-space is meaningful because of the prostration it hosts. As the governed noun of the assertive particle, it is held under a settled ownership claim before the ayah turns to spoken invocation. The premise also grounds the mosque-restriction logic seen in 9:18, and the dense plural sound gives way to a smoother dedication that gathers the many sites to one owner.

topics.headline: class-wide prostration-sites
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rule begins with all worship loci gathered together, not with a single mosque or isolated site.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a definite accusative plural noun of place, supporting class-wide scope in the ownership premise.

topics.headline: accusative subject under assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the worship-sites grammatically held inside a settled claim before human conduct is commanded.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the word as the governed noun of the assertive particle with a prepositional predicate completing the ownership claim.

topics.headline: bodily prostration inside the place noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the sacred site as a locus of bodily lowering, so the later vocal invocation is judged by the body's worship-orientation.
topics.reason: The local form tag is a noun of time or place from the prostration root, so the site and its worship-function remain linked.

topics.headline: mosque ownership formula field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects this ownership premise with the mosque-restriction logic of 9:18 while seeing 72:18 ground the rule in prior divine possession.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete recurrence evidence, and nothing in the local grammar contradicts reading 72:18 as the ownership premise beneath related mosque restrictions.

topics.headline: dense plural sound before dedication
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the many-site cluster give way to the smoother dedication that gathers them to one owner.
topics.reason: The sound observation is local to the visible surface and reinforces the same plural-to-one movement preserved by the grammatical topics.

words.gloss_range: preposition of belonging, dedication, and proper assignment in the ownership predicate
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) is the small relation-word that makes the worship-sites belong to God and be dedicated for Him. The premise is therefore not mere location or movement toward God; it is assignment and ownership. Its attached form makes the dedication look and sound joined to the divine name rather than detachable from it. That relation also sets up the ayah's contrast: rightful dedication is followed by a ban on placing any other in accompaniment with God.

topics.headline: belonging and dedication
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition turns sacred space into owned and dedicated space, so the later prohibition follows from assignment to God.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the prepositional phrase the predicate of the first clause, supporting possession and dedication rather than mere location.

topics.headline: attached form binds relation to the name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees and hears the dedication relation as tightly joined to the divine name rather than detachable from it.
topics.reason: The preposition is a proclitic in the local predicate, and the surface form supports the compressed ownership relation.

topics.headline: rightful dedication versus forbidden withness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the ayah's theology through two relational particles: one assigns worship-space to God, the other names the forbidden co-invocation relation.
topics.reason: The local syntax uses one preposition for the ownership predicate and another in the prohibition clause, creating the contrast pressed by the CRITICAL rows.

words.gloss_range: the divine proper name as genitive possessor and dedicatee in the first ownership predicate
words.root_gloss_range: worship, deityhood, awe, dependence, and deification pressure; local form is the proper divine name rather than a generic deity noun
words.prose: {{ar:لَّهِ}} ({{tr:llāhi}}) completes the ownership predicate as a genitive proper name. The sites are not assigned to a generic deity-class or to one participant among many; the proper name gives the premise its unique referent. No verb of assigning is narrated, so ownership is heard as already true. The broader root field adds worship and awe pressure, while local grammar keeps that pressure anchored in the name as owner and dedicatee. This first occurrence establishes ownership before the second bars shared invocation, and 72:19 then models the proper servant relation; the fused form keeps dedication compactly joined to the name.

topics.headline: proper name as possessor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the worship-sites are assigned to the unique proper divine referent, not to a generic or shareable deity category.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a genitive definite proper noun governed by the preceding preposition.

topics.headline: settled ownership without a verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears ownership as already true before any act of assigning or giving is narrated.
topics.reason: The first clause has a prepositional predicate with no overt copula, presenting belonging as a settled state.

topics.headline: worship and awe field anchored in the name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels ownership as worship-directed and awe-laden, while the local form remains the proper name rather than a free dictionary branch.
topics.reason: The root family supports worship and awe pressure, but the local word is a proper noun in a genitive predicate, so derivative meanings color the ownership claim rather than replacing the name.

topics.headline: first divine name sets the ayah frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first divine name establish ownership before the second occurrence bars shared invocation, with 72:19 modeling the proper servant relation.
topics.reason: The ayah repeats the divine name across two governed relations, and the same-surah rows connect that frame to the exclusive calling of 72:19.

topics.headline: dedication compressed into the name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the divine name compactly joined to the dedication relation that grounds the clause.
topics.reason: The local surface is the fused first divine-name occurrence after the ownership preposition.

words.gloss_range: causal and consequential connector deriving the prohibition from the ownership premise
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) turns the completed ownership premise into consequence. Once the worship-sites are God's, co-invocation is not merely discouraged; it becomes the contradiction that the next words forbid. Its tight connection to the negative command compresses reasoning and restraint into one decisive turn.

topics.headline: therefore from ownership to ban
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prohibition is derived from divine ownership rather than appended as an unrelated command.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the second clause as a result following the first ownership clause.

topics.headline: nominal theology becomes verbal discipline
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah pivot from a statement about sacred space into a direct regulation of address.
topics.reason: The connector sits exactly between the nominal ownership clause and the verbal prohibition clause.

topics.headline: compressed consequence-command surface
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees and hears the prohibition launch as the immediate surface continuation of the causal connector.
topics.reason: The proclitic is joined directly to the following negative particle, making consequence and prohibition one local onset.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive negation governing the jussive plural verb and scoping over the whole co-invocation structure
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is prohibitive, so the ayah regulates practice rather than reporting that a mistake is absent. Its scope does not stop at the verb; it stretches through the accompaniment phrase to the final indefinite object. The result is a direct communal restraint over any act of invoking another with God.

topics.headline: direct prohibition over practice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause commands a stopped practice rather than merely describing monotheism.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as negative and the following verb as jussive; translation support identifies the construction as prohibition.

topics.headline: scope reaches the final object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks one negative command across the whole co-invocation configuration, all the way to the final anyone.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence keeps the accompaniment phrase and direct object inside the same prohibition clause.

topics.headline: external negative governor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the act visibly governed from outside, with the negative command dependent on the causal turn before it.
topics.reason: The particle remains separate before the verb while being joined in the local surface to the causal connector.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural jussive invocation or calling, locally narrowed to worship-directed address forbidden with another recipient beside God
words.root_gloss_range: calling, summoning, inviting, supplicating, and claim-making extensions; local frame selects worship-directed invocation under prohibition
words.prose: {{ar:تَدْعُوا۟}} ({{tr:tadʿū}}) carries a plural audience inside the verb, so the prohibition addresses communal speech-practice without needing an explicit pronoun. The root's calling and supplication range is narrowed here by the accompaniment phrase and final object: the forbidden act is not ordinary speech, but worship-directed co-address. Claim-language in the root family adds pressure because invoking another this way effectively assigns that other a share in sacred address, while the local Form I verb remains direct calling. The same root then reappears as corrected exclusive address in 72:19 and 72:20, after the plural ban has cleared the field. The vocal act is also constrained by the earlier prostration-site premise, and its long sound projects outward until the grammar supplies the forbidden relation.

topics.headline: plural jussive address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a whole addressee group has its repeatable invocation practice placed under command.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as jussive second-person masculine plural, and attachment evidence supplies the implicit plural subject.

topics.headline: calling defined by co-address frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the verb becomes prohibited because its complements create co-address with God, not because all calling is forbidden.
topics.reason: The verb has an explicit object and an accompaniment phrase in the same prohibition clause, selecting worship-directed invocation as the local issue.

topics.headline: calling as enacted claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels that co-invocation makes a status-claim about the addressee, while local grammar still selects direct calling rather than a separate claim verb.
topics.reason: Dictionary evidence supports claim-related derivatives, but the local surface is a Form I jussive call verb, so the claim force remains semantic pressure inside the act of invocation.

topics.headline: plural ban answered by exclusive calling
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the plural prohibition in 72:18 answered by modeled exclusive calling in 72:19 and 72:20.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete same-surah recurrence, and the local prohibition prepares the corrected invocation in 72:19 and 72:20.

topics.headline: voice constrained by worship-space
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels spoken invocation governed by the earlier prostration-site premise, with the sound of the call extending until the grammar supplies the forbidden relation.
topics.reason: The word follows the ownership premise and precedes the accompaniment phrase, so its vocal action is structurally tied to sacred-space ownership.

words.gloss_range: adverbial accompaniment and associative withness defining the forbidden co-invocation relation
words.root_gloss_range: withness, accompaniment, association, and simultaneity; local use is the relational adverb governing the following divine name
words.prose: {{ar:مَعَ}} ({{tr:maʿa}}) is the hinge that turns calling into forbidden co-address. It does not describe replacement of God by another; it names the subtler addition of another recipient alongside Him in the act of invocation. The relation opens before the final object arrives, so that object is defined by attempted placement with God. Because the word is a simple relational adverb, the theological force rests on placement: withness itself is the relation excluded. It mirrors the earlier rightful dedication relation, and its nasal opening helps frame the accompaniment phrase before the final indefinite closure.

topics.headline: withness defines the forbidden relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the error is adding another recipient into worship with God, not only replacing God with an alternative.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the word as an adverbial accompaniment phrase modifying the calling event.

topics.headline: relation opens before anyone is named
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the forbidden relation open before the final object arrives, so the final anyone is defined by attempted placement with God.
topics.reason: The adverbial relation is positioned between the verb and the divine-name complement, before the direct object closes the clause.

topics.headline: simple adverb carries the weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that a small function word, not a rich verbal derivation, carries the clause's decisive theological geometry.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as an adverb, and contextual evidence shows its distribution dominated by adverbial accompaniment.

topics.headline: withness against rightful dedication
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the ayah's contrast between rightful dedication to God and the forbidden relation of invoking another with God.
topics.reason: The local clause contrasts the ownership preposition with the accompaniment adverb, and the CRITICAL rows tie that contrast to anti-co-invocation formula pressure.

topics.headline: nasal opening of the companion phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the accompaniment phrase as a compact relational frame before the final indefinite closure.
topics.reason: The sound row is local to the surface and reinforces the same accompaniment relation preserved by the syntactic topics.

words.gloss_range: the divine proper name as genitive complement of the accompaniment word, fixed before the excluded object
words.root_gloss_range: worship, deityhood, awe, dependence, and deification pressure; local form is the proper divine name under accompaniment syntax
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) is governed here by the accompaniment word, not by the earlier ownership preposition. That changed governor makes the repeated name do new work: God is now the fixed, non-shareable reference beside whom no other may be placed. The proper name resists becoming one coordinate in a pair, and its position before the indefinite object lets divine identifiability fill the relation before any possible other is named. At this co-address point, the worship-recipient field is concentrated but remains anchored in the proper name. The repeated name moves from dedication to forbidden accompaniment and then toward the proper servant relation in 72:19, while the uniqueness confession of 112:1 is inverted into a ban on any co-invoked one.

topics.headline: governed by withness, not ownership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second divine-name occurrence belongs to the forbidden accompaniment phrase, not to the earlier ownership predicate.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks this word as the genitive complement governed by the accompaniment adverb.

topics.headline: proper name refuses pairing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the impossible geometry of placing a proper divine name into a pair with an invoked other.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a definite proper noun, while the local construction names accompaniment only to prohibit any other from entering it.

topics.headline: worship field at co-address point
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the worship-recipient field concentrated at the point where shared address is denied, while the local word remains the proper name.
topics.reason: Root-family evidence supports worship and deification pressure, but the local form is the proper divine name governed by the accompaniment phrase.

topics.headline: divine name before excluded anyone
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears God occupy the relation before the final indefinite opens the class of every excluded other.
topics.reason: The word stands between the accompaniment adverb and the final accusative object.

topics.headline: second occurrence closes the mirror
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the repeated divine name from rightful dedication to forbidden accompaniment, then into the proper servant relation in 72:19.
topics.reason: The two divine-name occurrences have different governors in 72:18, and the CRITICAL rows give a concrete continuation in 72:19.

topics.headline: uniqueness formula inverted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the uniqueness confession of 112:1 inverted here into a prohibition against any co-invoked one.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply the concrete 112:1 echo, and local syntax uses the divine name before the excluded final object.

words.gloss_range: accusative indefinite anyone as the explicit object of the prohibited invocation, giving the ban exhaustive reach
words.root_gloss_range: oneness, singularity, any-one force, aloneness, and declaring unity; local use is an indefinite object under prohibition
words.prose: {{ar:أَحَدًۭا}} ({{tr:aḥadan}}) closes the ayah as an accusative indefinite object, so the ban reaches any possible co-invoked recipient. Its case keeps it tied to the calling verb rather than making it an apposition to the preceding divine name. Negation, withness, and the unrestricted object work together, so each possible partner is tested one by one and excluded. The root's oneness field becomes exclusion here: the smallest imaginable one stands for every possible other, reversing the positive uniqueness formula of 112:1 into a negative ban. The final position leaves no loophole after the relation with God has already been named, and 72:20 continues the same exclusivity as a first-person confession.

topics.headline: anyone as governed object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word is the forbidden invoked object, not an apposition to the divine name or a companion governed by the withness phrase.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as accusative indefinite, and attachment evidence marks it as the direct object of the calling verb.

topics.headline: indefinite under prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prohibition become exhaustive because negation, withness, and an unrestricted object work together.
topics.reason: The negative command scopes over the accompaniment phrase and the indefinite direct object, giving the clause universal exclusion.

topics.headline: one-at-a-time exclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels each possible partner tested one by one and excluded, rather than a vague collective category being dismissed.
topics.reason: The local noun is singular and indefinite under negation, and the root field supports any-one and singularity force.

topics.headline: uniqueness language reversed into exclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the positive uniqueness formula of 112:1 turned in 72:18 into a negative exclusion of every co-invoked one.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give the concrete 112:1 echo, and local grammar changes the oneness language into an indefinite object under prohibition.

topics.headline: final word closes every loophole
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the universal object only after God has occupied the relation, so the ayah closes by excluding every remaining possible other.
topics.reason: The final object is delayed until after the accompaniment phrase and divine name, giving the clause its closing universal force.

topics.headline: exclusive worship continues nearby
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects the excluded anyone here with the same-surah exclusivity that continues in 72:20.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows identify same-surah recurrence and a closing sound-sense pair that reinforce exclusive address.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The predicate al-masajid li-llah is followed by fa-la tad'u ma'a Allah ahadan, making exclusive address a consequence of divine ownership.
baseline_models.mechanism: Prayer sites form a devotional domain owned by Allah; calling draws an addressee into that domain, while ahadan under negation exhausts every possible additional recipient.

activation_trace.role: The prostration-place image makes al-masajid a set of devotional sites whose stated ownership governs their use.
Worship and the worshipped one identify Allah as both owner and sole devotional recipient.
Calling that draws near by speech supplies the act whose recipient must remain singular.
Negative exhaustive 'anyone' closes the domain to every additional addressee without exception.

changed_reading.before: The ayah says that mosques belong to Allah and forbids polytheistic prayer.
changed_reading.after: Every place of prostration is an exclusively addressed domain: because it is Allah's, no call may draw a second recipient into worship alongside Him.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The plural al-masajid can remain attached to the prostrating body through the inventory's limbs-and-mark branch, while li-llah assigns those sites to Allah.
baseline_models.mechanism: The body's several contact points become a distributed sanctuary. Divine ownership allocates the full embodied act, and the exhaustive prohibition leaves no bodily gesture available for a second devotional recipient.

activation_trace.role: The prostration-limbs and prostration-mark image supplies an anatomical sense for the plural sites.
The worship image makes bodily allocation devotional rather than merely anatomical.
Directed calling joins bodily submission to a named recipient.
Exhaustive negation prevents even one alternate recipient from receiving part of the embodied act.

changed_reading.before: Al-masajid denotes buildings reserved for divine worship.
changed_reading.after: The whole embodied apparatus of prostration is reserved for Allah, so voice and limb cannot be partitioned between Him and another.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The lowering and steady-gaze branches of s-j-d combine with tad'u as speech that draws a recipient near.
baseline_models.mechanism: Submission coordinates posture, gaze, and voice into one vector. Calling another 'with' Allah would split that vector even if the outward posture still looked devotional.

activation_trace.role: Humbled lowering supplies the submissive posture whose direction is at issue.
The steady lowered gaze contributes sustained attention and makes divided inward orientation visible.
The call's drawing force gives the attentive posture a directional verbal outlet.
Exhaustive negation rules out every competing direction of attention.

changed_reading.before: The prohibition concerns the named object of supplication.
changed_reading.after: It also regulates attentional integrity: lowered body, sustained gaze, and spoken call must converge rather than divide across recipients.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The claim-or-affiliation branch of d-'-w can attach to tad'u, while ma'a places the forbidden other in a co-position with Allah.
baseline_models.mechanism: A sacred domain can be compromised not only by prayer to another but by asserting that a person, lineage, or institution holds a right or affiliation alongside its divine owner.

activation_trace.role: Claiming a right or affiliation broadens the prohibited call into a social or legal assertion of co-entitlement.
The prayer-site image supplies the domain over which a rival claim could be asserted.
The worshipped-one image fixes the domain's entitlement in Allah.
Exhaustive negation excludes every candidate co-claimant.

changed_reading.before: Do not verbally invoke a second deity in a mosque.
changed_reading.after: Do not install any human or institution as a co-entitled affiliate within a worship domain that belongs to Allah.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier human-to-jinn refuge relation produces an increase in engulfing burden. The focus prohibition then reads as a causal intervention: exclusive calling prevents secondary protectors from becoming a self-reinforcing dependency system.

activation_trace.role: Seeking refuge and protective attachment supplies the concrete secondary-agent dependency.
Increase and growth turn the refuge relation into an escalating process rather than a static mistake.
Engulfing and overpowering supplies the harmful output that the dependency amplifies.
Calling that draws an addressee near anchors the proposed intervention in the focus command.
Exhaustive negation blocks every candidate secondary protector.

structural_cues: 72:6 sequences refuge in agents before an explicit increase in rahaq.
72:18 uses fa after divine ownership to issue the no-call command.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies refuge, increase, and engulfment; I infer that redirected dependence is the causal arrow and that exclusive calling interrupts it. A live alternative is that 72:6 is only an example of error and 72:18 states the rule without a feedback claim.

changed_reading.before: The focus gives a categorical ban on invoking another.
changed_reading.after: The ban also breaks a protection racket of the spirit: treating another agent as refuge increases the very burden from which protection is sought.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context moves from multiple extended paths cut into divergent groups to conditional straightness on the path. Against that social plurality, plural masajid under one owner become a unifying network rather than properties of competing paths.

activation_trace.role: The extended-path image supplies the routes along which communities organize themselves.
Divergent paths and groups make the social and directional fragmentation explicit.
Straightness and even alignment supply the counter-motion that can reconnect divided routes.
Plural prayer sites provide common nodes across otherwise divided routes.
The single worshipped owner prevents each path from installing its own sacred claimant.

structural_cues: 72:11 juxtaposes plural paths with their being cut into divergent kinds.
72:16 shifts to conditional straightness on a singular way, while 72:18 retains plural masajid under singular ownership.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies divided routes, straightness, plural worship sites, and one owner; I infer that common ownership reconnects socially divided routes without erasing their plurality. Alternatively, the route material may describe moral classes without organizing the mosque plural.

changed_reading.before: Each mosque is individually reserved for Allah.
changed_reading.after: Across communities split into different routes, the many worship sites form one divine domain and cannot be captured by a path-specific patron.

context_deltas.mechanism: Water is supplied in abundance and immediately framed as an assay; turning away follows as the failed response. The focus then governs attribution under prosperity: provision may test whom recipients address, but it does not create a rival patron with a claim on worship.

activation_trace.role: Giving drink and quenching supplies the beneficent transfer that can attract loyalty.
Water's appearance, entry, and abundance make the provision materially pervasive.
Copious water and provision intensify the gift beyond mere sufficiency.
Assaying metal or a person recasts abundance as a test that reveals orientation.
Turning one's side away supplies the failed directional response to the test.
The worshipped-one image fixes the true patron despite the intervening material means.
Directed calling is the observable allocation of gratitude and dependence under the test.

structural_cues: 72:16 makes abundant watering the consequence of straightness.
72:17 immediately gives that abundance a testing purpose before describing a turn away.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies provision, abundance, assay, and turning away; I infer that prosperity tests attribution and can tempt recipients to address a visible means as patron. A live alternative is that the test concerns conduct generally, not the recipient of invocation specifically.

changed_reading.before: Exclusive invocation protects worship from rival deities.
changed_reading.after: Exclusive invocation also protects attribution during abundance: a gift or its visible channel must not be promoted into a co-patron of the worship site.

context_deltas.mechanism: A servant stands and calls Him while a crowd nearly becomes a piled mass over the human caller. The focus partitions physical gathering around a messenger from devotional address: proximity, density, and charisma must not turn the caller into a co-recipient.

activation_trace.role: Bodily standing places the servant visibly at the center of the scene.
Submissive worship defines the central human as servant rather than sovereign recipient.
Calling that draws near specifies that the servant's own address is directed to Him.
Near-realization marks the crowd configuration as an imminent but not completed conversion of the scene.
A dense mass layered upon itself supplies the social pressure concentrated around the servant.
The communal prayer-site image anchors the crowd mechanism in a worship assembly.
Exhaustive negation bars the central servant as decisively as any remote rival.

structural_cues: 72:19 follows the focus directly and contrasts the servant's singular upward call with a plural crowd gathering over him.
The pronouns distinguish the one being called from the human body around which the crowd accumulates.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a standing servant, his call to Him, and an almost-piled crowd; I infer that human-centered density can redirect devotional attention toward the caller. The crowd could instead be hostile or merely eager, but either alternative still requires separating proximity to the messenger from calling upon him.

changed_reading.before: No second divine figure may be invoked in a sacred place.
changed_reading.after: Even when a worship assembly physically centers on a compelling human caller, the crowd may gather around him but may not convert him into a co-addressee.

context_deltas.mechanism: The speaker disclaims ownership of harm and right direction, then denies that anyone can shelter him from Allah or provide an alternate refuge. These capacity denials explain why adding a human recipient to invocation is not only disloyal but functionally misplaced.

activation_trace.role: Ownership and power of disposal supply the capacity the messenger explicitly denies possessing.
Harm and deficiency name one outcome over which the human speaker disclaims control.
Rightly hitting the proper course names the beneficial outcome he likewise cannot dispose.
Protective neighborhood and shelter supply the rescue capacity denied to every agent against Allah.
Exhaustive 'no one' universalizes the absence of a protecting intermediary.
Inclining toward a refuge depicts the alternate shelter that cannot be found.
Calling as directed attraction anchors the capacity argument in the focus prohibition.
The worshipped-one branch identifies where effective dependence and devotion terminate.

structural_cues: 72:21 pairs two negated outcome nouns under the speaker's negated ownership.
72:22 expands the denial from the speaker's power to every possible protector and every alternate refuge.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit denials of disposal, protection, and refuge; I infer that invocation ordinarily assigns expected efficacy and therefore must not be routed to the powerless messenger. A live alternative is that invocation can be honorific without assigning efficacy, though the local capacity sequence presses against that separation.

changed_reading.before: Exclusive calling is demanded because Allah alone deserves worship.
changed_reading.after: Exclusive calling also tracks actual agency: the messenger transmits but owns neither harmful nor beneficial outcomes and cannot function as an alternate shelter.

context_deltas.mechanism: Hidden knowledge is not exposed to anyone except an approved messenger, whose route is guarded and whose task is delivery under complete divine cognizance. This distinguishes authorized mediation from shared invocation: a messenger may carry disclosure without becoming a devotional co-recipient.

activation_trace.role: Concealment from sight supplies the protected information domain.
Emergence and disclosure supply the controlled crossing from hidden to manifest.
Exhaustive negation closes disclosure to everyone before the stated exception.
Acceptance and approval supply the authorization criterion for the exceptional messenger.
Messenger and message define the human as a transmission role rather than a worship endpoint.
Watchful guarding protects the authorized channel around the messenger.
Delivering the message fixes the channel's purpose in successful transmission.
Complete encompassing in knowledge and custody keeps authorization under divine control.
Directed calling supplies the distinct devotional channel that must terminate in Allah.
The same exhaustive exclusion prevents the authorized carrier from becoming an added addressee.

structural_cues: 72:26-27 uses a closed-to-anyone construction followed by an explicit approved-messenger exception.
72:27 places guards before and behind the messenger, and 72:28 gives delivery rather than independent disposal as his function.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies concealed knowledge, controlled disclosure, approval, messengerhood, guarding, delivery, and encompassing custody; I infer two distinct routes, revelation through a messenger and invocation to Allah. The alternative is that the closing sequence concerns only epistemic security, but it still prevents messenger access from implying devotional partnership.

changed_reading.before: Calling Allah alone excludes every intermediary from religion.
changed_reading.after: The ayah excludes co-address, not authorized transmission: the messenger can be an approved, guarded carrier of disclosure while never becoming a recipient alongside Allah.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing sequence combines exhaustive enumeration, total enclosure, and counted particulars. It activates the anatomical branch of masajid as a complete inventory: every prostrating member is already accounted for within divine ownership, leaving no embodied remainder for another.

activation_trace.role: Enumeration by number and exhaustive survey supply item-by-item accounting.
Totality as encompassing completion closes the inventory around the whole embodied set.
Counting the numbered particulars makes each member inspectable rather than treating the body as an undifferentiated whole.
The prostration-limbs image provides the countable embodied members to which the closing totality can return.
Exhaustive negation leaves not even one member's devotion assignable elsewhere.

structural_cues: 72:28 closes the surah with a threefold totalizing sequence: encompassing, exhaustive counting, and every thing by number.
The focus uses a plural prostration noun and closes its prohibition with exhaustive ahadan.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies prostration limbs plus complete enumeration; I infer that the closing totality retroactively inventories the body's multiple masajid under one owner. A live alternative is that 72:28 is only a universal knowledge claim with no anatomical callback.

changed_reading.before: The embodied reading generally dedicates the body to Allah.
changed_reading.after: The dedication is distributive and audited: every prostrating member is individually encompassed, so no single limb, mark, or gesture is left for a rival recipient.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates a specialized image-coin and tribute branch rather than the ordinary mosque sense. It remains anchored directly in the packet's s-j-d inventory and gains a live material analogy from the messenger's denial of ownership; downstream prose should present it only as an exploratory warning about material or royal proxies, never as the lexical gloss of al-masajid or a historical claim about 72:18.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus inventory includes image-bearing coins before which prostration is made and tribute under s-j-d, while the focus assigns masajid to Allah.

activation_trace.role: Image-coins before which prostration occurs supply a material token capable of carrying royal or iconic authority into devotion.
Tribute and tribute-coins add an economic submission image to the material proxy.
Ownership and disposal, explicitly denied by the human speaker, prevent a material or royal token from inheriting effective sacred ownership.
The worshipped-one image keeps devotion fixed on Allah rather than the token that represents authority.

changed_reading.before: The ayah protects mosques from alternate objects of prayer.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, it also resists turning images, money, tribute, or royal tokens into proxies that receive the submission owed to Allah.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the non-dominant d-'-' mapping's rough-thrust branch for a QAC d-'-w form. It remains packet-resolvable and is anchored by the piled crowd immediately after the focus; downstream prose must label it a kinetic social-pressure analogy, not parse tad'u as 'push' or replace the ordinary calling sense.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The split focus inventory permits a forceful-driving image for tad'u, and 72:19 supplies a dense crowd nearly layered over the servant.

activation_trace.role: Rough thrusting or forceful driving supplies the outlier's kinetic image of social pressure moving a person into a forbidden co-position.
Handling something with severity intensifies the crowd's near-action into pressure rather than neutral proximity.
A piled, overlapping multitude supplies the collective body that exerts the pressure.
Exhaustive negation marks every human candidate as forbidden from being driven into a place alongside Allah.

changed_reading.before: The command forbids choosing another recipient of invocation.
changed_reading.after: As a contained kinetic analogy, it also forbids collective pressure from driving a revered human into the devotional position beside Allah.

strongest_changes: The refuge-in-jinn sequence turns exclusive invocation into an intervention against an escalating dependency loop.
The piled crowd around the calling servant separates physical or charismatic centrality from devotional recipient status.
The messenger's capacity denials show that transmission does not confer ownership of harm, guidance, protection, or refuge.
The guarded disclosure sequence distinguishes authorized mediation through a messenger from invocation directed to Allah.
The closing enumeration strengthens the reading of masajid as every embodied prostration member individually assigned to Allah.
summary.what_was_special: The ownership-to-prohibition construction became a routing rule across spatial, social, material, epistemic, and bodily systems: the context repeatedly tests who receives address, who merely carries a message, and what happens when a secondary agent is treated as protector, patron, or co-owner.
remaining_uncertainties: The place-of-prostration and limbs-of-prostration readings remain coexisting senses; the context activates both but does not force a choice.
The crowd in 72:19 may be eager, hostile, or simply dense, so the recipient-partition model is stronger than any claim about its motive.
The abundance model depends on an inferred temptation to misattribute visible provision, not an explicit context statement.
The numismatic and coercive readings are deliberately retained as branch-distant analogies and must not be rendered as ordinary lexical senses.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Places of lowering belong exclusively to God.** `المساجد` activates س ج د B001-B003, humble lowering, prayer sites, and prostrating limbs; both divine names activate ء ل ه B001-B002; `تدعوا` activates د ع و B001, calling to draw near; and `أحدا` activates ء ح د B002, exhaustive anyone. Ownership (`لله`) precedes prohibition, so the institutional site, bodily act, and addressed call are brought under one relation. The inferred mechanism is that exclusive ownership entails exclusive direction. The ayah reads the mosque not merely as property but as an integrated field of posture, place, and invocation.

2. **Co-invocation can also be a rival claim of affiliation.** د ع و B002 means claiming a right or affiliation, activated by `مع الله`. The packet later has the servant call upon God amid a gathering (72:19) and explicitly deny partnership (72:20). The inferred move is that adding another caller is also adding another claim upon the worship relation. The prohibition therefore reaches both vocal appeal and institutional co-ownership.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The standing servant’s call in 72:19 and his explicit no-partnership declaration in 72:20 enact the rule in person. The later sequence joins owned place, embodied worship, and exclusive address without adding a rival claimant.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Plural sites have one jurisdiction.** Fixed `س ج د` B002 is a prostration/prayer site and communal place; the plural `ٱلْمَسَاجِدَ` is predicated `لِلَّهِ`, with fixed `ء ل ه` B001 identifying worship and the worshipped one. The local window has moved from many paths (72:11), to one path (72:16), to multiple worship sites here; I infer that spatial plurality does not distribute ultimate ownership. The clause reads as a jurisdictional rule: every lowering-place belongs to the same addressee.

2. **The place is defined by the posture it hosts.** Fixed `س ج د` B001 is humble lowering and submission, while B002 names the site from that act. In 72:19 the servant `قَامَ` to call, placing standing service beside prostrating space; in 72:14 surrender likewise preceded deliberate action. The packet supplies lowering, site, standing, and surrender; I infer that the location's ownership follows the orientation enacted there, not its architecture alone. `ٱلْمَسَاجِد` reads as spaces constituted by exclusive submission.

3. **Calling would draw an unauthorized party into shared ritual space.** Fixed `د ع و` B001 is calling that draws another near by speech; fixed `ش ر ك` B001 in the nearby declarations (72:20) is bringing another into shared participation, and `مَعَ` supplies co-presence. The packet supplies calling, drawing-near, shared participation, and the site's exclusive ownership; I infer that invocation is spatially consequential: it installs an additional party inside the relation. `فَلَا تَدْعُوا مَعَ ٱللَّهِ` reads as refusal to populate worship with a co-recipient.

4. **Claimed affiliation is also excluded.** Fixed `د ع و` B002 includes claiming a right, lineage, or affiliation. The earlier denial of divine consort/offspring is outside this fixed focus window, but within it 72:20 repeats `أَدْعُوا رَبِّي وَلَا أُشْرِكُ`, and 72:22 rejects any alternative protector or refuge. The packet supplies exclusive invocation and no alternative affiliation; I infer that the prohibition covers not only vocal address but any claim that gives another a right "with" God. This is a secondary branch, anchored in the fixed verb.

5. **`أَحَدًا` audits every site and every possible co-recipient.** Fixed `ء ح د` B002 is exhaustive anyone under negation and B005 distributes individuals one by one. The plural sites could invite local exceptions; the singular indefinite closes them. The packet supplies spatial plurality and exhaustive negation; I infer a site-by-site, candidate-by-candidate exclusion. The ending reads as a universal constraint with no local exemption.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 72:20 supplies the fixed prohibition's exact positive model: the servant calls his Lord and does not install any partner. Ayat 72:21-23 then prevent exclusive calling from becoming messenger-centered power by denying his ownership, refuge, and any role beyond delivery. Thus every `س ج د` B002 site has one jurisdiction, but the human carrier within it remains a servant rather than a co-recipient.

baseline.text: Mescitler Allah'a aittir; öyleyse Allah ile birlikte hiç kimseye yakarmayın.

findings.text: Mescitler, bina olmanın ötesinde bedenin alçalması, ibadet yeri ve yakarışın yöneldiği muhatabı tek sahiplik alanında birleştirir.
Allah ile birlikte başka birine yakarmak, onu yalnız seslenilen biri değil, ibadet ilişkisinde hak ve ortaklık iddia eden bir taraf olarak içeri alır.
Çoğul ibadet yerleriyle tekil ve belirsiz hiç kimsenin birleşmesi, yasağı her yerde ve her olası muhatap bakımından işleterek hiçbir yerel istisna bırakmaz.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi başı alçaltıp bedeni eğme, binmek için bineği alçaltma, belden eğilmiş duruş ve meyve yüküyle ağacın yana yatması örneklerini açıkça verir. Geçici çerçeve bu aşağı yönlü eğilme çekirdeğini doğru taşır; insan hareketi ile yük altında oluşan eğilme ayrı yüzler olarak tutulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal aşağı doğru eğilme ve yükle yatmayı kapsar; alnın yere konmasını, bağlılık tutumunu veya bakışın uzun süre tutulmasını zorunlu kılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam karışık ve çıplak olmayan türdedir; insanın eğilmesi, bineğin alçaltılması ve yüklü ağacın yatması ayrı biçimlere bağlı yüzlerdir.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanın başını alçaltıp gövdesini öne eğmesi ya da binmeye elverişli olsun diye bir bineğin alçaltılmasıdır. Cansız uzantıda ise ağır meyve yükünün ağacı eğip yana yatırması anlatılır.

facets.statement: İnsanla ilgili temel kullanım, başı alçaltıp gövdeyi öne doğru eğmektir.
Ettirgen kullanımda binek hayvanı, üzerine binilebilmesi için aşağı alçaltılır.
Bir açıklama, insan duruşunu özellikle belden öne eğilmiş olma biçimiyle karşılar.
Ağaca aktarılan kullanımda ağır meyve yükü gövdeyi veya dalları eğip yana yatırır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar başı alçaltma ve gövdeyi eğme çekirdeğinde birleşir; bineği binmek için alçaltma bu çekirdeğin ettirgen biçimidir. Meyve yüküyle ağacın eğilmesi ise aynı aşağı yönlü biçimin cansız varlığa uzantısıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bakışı aşağı yönelmiş durumda uzun süre tutmayı, gözün devinimsizliğini ve göz kapaklarındaki gevşekliği birlikte tanıklar. Geçici çerçeve, kısa bir bakıştan veya yalnızca baş eğmeden farklı olan bu süreklilik ve durgunluk bileşenlerini doğru yansıtır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal bakışın sürmesi, aşağı yönelmesi ve göz kapaklarının gevşekliğiyle sınırlıdır; yere kapanma hareketini veya yalnızca güçlü bakışı anlatmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam karışık ve çıplak olmayan türdedir; eylem adı ile durgun göz ve gevşek bakışlı kadınları anlatan bağlı kullanımlar ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bakışı aşağı yönelmiş biçimde uzun süre ve devinimsiz tutmak, buna eşlik eden göz kapağı durgunluğu ve gevşek bakış görünümüdür. Kadın veya göz nitelemesinde bu görünüm, bakışın sakin ve güçsüz oluşunu belirtir.

facets.statement: Temel eylem, bakışı aşağı yönelmiş durumda uzun süre ve devinimsiz tutmaktır.
Gözle ilgili nitelemede göz kapaklarının gevşekliği ve bakışın sakin, durgun görünümü öne çıkar.
Kadınları niteleyen çoğul kullanım, gözlerin gevşek ve durgun görünmesini anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar bakışın uzun sürmesi ve gözün devinimsizliği üzerinde birleşir; bazı açıklamalar aşağı yönelme ve göz kapaklarındaki gevşekliği belirginleştirir. Göz ve kadın nitelemelerinde aynı görünüm sakin, güçsüz ve durgun bakış olarak gerçekleşir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, üzerinde betimler bulunan ve görüldüklerinde önlerinde eğilinilen belirli sikkeleri ortak biçimde tanıklar. Ancak eğilmenin doğrudan betime mi yoksa betimde gösterilen hükümdara mı yöneldiği kaynak anlatımlarında farklı kurulabildiğinden dal kimliği bu hedef ayrımı belirtilerek kabul edilebilir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnızca betimli ve önünde eğilme davranışıyla tanımlanan sikke adlandırmasına bağlıdır; genel sikke, vergi parası veya her betimli nesne bu kapsama girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam yalnızca söz öbeğidir; tanım bu özel sikke adlandırmasına bağlı kalır ve bunu çıplak kökün genel para anlamı gibi sunmaz.

concept_map.definition: Üzerlerinde hükümdar betimleri ya da başka betimler bulunan ve görüldüklerinde betimlerin veya betimlenen hükümdarın önünde eğilinilen belirli sikkelerdir. Adlandırmanın ayırt edici yanı para olmaları değil, betim ile eğilme davranışı arasındaki bağdır.

facets.statement: Söz öbeği, üzerinde hükümdar veya başka bir varlık betimi bulunan belirli sikkeleri adlandırır.
Bu sikkeler görüldüğünde insanlar üzerlerindeki betimle bağlantılı olarak eğilme davranışı gösterir.
Eğilmenin hedefi kimi anlatımda betimin kendisi, kimi anlatımda ise betimde gösterilen hükümdardır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, üzerlerinde betimler bulunan ve görüldüklerinde eğilme davranışına konu olan belirli sikkelerde birleşir. Anlatımlar, bu davranışın betimin kendisine mi yoksa betimde gösterilen hükümdara mı yöneldiğini farklı biçimde kurar.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi iki bağlı süreci açıkça verir: duvarların birbiri ardından çökmesi ve yapıların birbiri ardından yıkılması. Hazırlanan çerçeve, ardışıklığı ve çökme ile ettirgen yıkma ayrımını korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi dönemin değişimlerini ve olayların yönünü değiştirmelerini anlatır. Hazırlanan çerçevenin olaylar ve yön verme bölümü uygundur, ancak insanın bu olaylara eğilmesi kaynakta kurucu bir katılımcı olarak açıkça verilmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam yalnızca dönemin yön verici değişimleri yapısına bağlıdır; yalın biçime genel bir olay veya çağırma anlamı yüklenmez.

concept_map.definition: Dönemin olayların akışını başka yöne çeviren değişimleri ve getirdiği gelişmelerdir. Yöneltme düşüncesi burada sesli bir çağrı değil, olayların seyrine etki eden mecazlı bir güçtür.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi iki yakın görünümü birlikte aktarır: iki hurma ağacı arasındaki açıklık ve seyrek duran hurma ağaçları. Ayrıca sözcüğün ilk ünsüzünün başka bir biçimde aktarılmış olabileceği belirtilir; bu nedenle dal hem yerleşim anlamını hem yazım belirsizliğini korumalıdır.

word_morpheme_spans.note: word_analysis critical words are orthographic/analytic units, not QAC words; each resolves to a MORPHEME SPAN. Use word_morpheme_spans for any word-level join to QAC.

word_analysis_qac_alignment.note: aligned_qac_word_ref does NOT resolve against qac_morphemes for this ayah: word-analysis counts orthographic words where QAC counts morphological words. Word-level joins between word_analysis topics and QAC morphology are UNRELIABLE here. Upstream defect in quran-data's word-analysis; deliberately not auto-repaired (renumbering would fabricate identities).

channel_review.note: first-pass blind review by a single reader; no adjudication, no accept/reject, no per-ayah channel maturity. Not a channel ledger.

channel_generated_outputs.note: Generated network-v3 channel discovery/family/path outputs are available as external quran-data files; read them only when channel detail is necessary, and do not treat them as an adjudicated channel ledger.

full_context_packet.note: surah-scope fallback: the default commentary workflow does not consume per-ayah focus packets, so the source packet is scoped by this builder to roots this ayah can justify and carries no staged reveal order

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.
